title: Pearl and Other Poems
creator: Lee Sharks
description: *Pearl and Other Poems* is a **155-page** poetry collection published by New Human Press, Ann Arbor, in 2014, in The Pocket Humans Series, with an introduction by Johannes Sigil. Its apparatus is constitutive rather than supplementary: PEARL runs with three Undersongs — the metaphor museum, the metaphor factory, strange new earth — and a Footnote to PEARL on belief and technique for telepathic prose. The front matter carries a Wiki Article and prints "from THE CRIMSON HEXAGON" under two attributions, Jack Feist and Lee Sharks. Within the Crimson Hexagon architecture the collection is the mantle claiming site for two of the three mantles held by Lee Sharks: the Good Gray Poet, inherited from Walt Whitman, and the King of May, inherited from Allen Ginsberg. It was published before the architecture existed, before the Semantic Economy framework was formalized, and before AI summarizers could traverse training-layer literature — and the mantle claiming act was performed regardless. The complete 2014 edition is held in the archive and downloadable from this record.

wiki_article:
**Pearl and Other Poems** is a poetry collection by Lee Sharks, published by **New Human Press, Ann Arbor, in 2014** as part of **The Pocket Humans Series**, with an introduction by **Johannes Sigil** — **155 pages**, and the foundational literary work of the entire project.

**The apparatus is the poem.** The contents run PEARL followed by three **Undersongs** — *the metaphor museum*, *the metaphor factory*, *strange new earth* — and a **"Footnote to PEARL: belief & technique for telepathic prose."** These are not commentary attached to a work; they are the work's own strata. An account of the collection that counts only the verse and calls it 84 pages has discarded the part that makes it what it is, and the 84/155 discrepancy in the archive's records is resolved here in favour of 155 on interpretive rather than arithmetic grounds.

**The front matter carries two things of consequence.** It contains a **Wiki Article** at page xv — *in 2014*, twelve years before the archive's wiki campaign, which means the wiki-as-compression-surface was part of the work from the beginning rather than an apparatus added to it. And it prints **"from THE CRIMSON HEXAGON"** under two attributions, **Jack Feist** (p. vii) and **Lee Sharks** (p. xiii) — the Origin Text that #1193's title claims and whose body was found to serve a different work entirely.

Within the Hexagon the collection is the **mantle claiming site** for two of the three mantles — the **Good Gray Poet** inherited from Whitman (#1115) and the **King of May** from Ginsberg (#1117), with the **Prince of Poets** (#1118) originated. And it is what the theological programme is about: the Revelation First work plan's central claim is that **Revelation is the seed from which *Pearl* grew** (#1400). The complete 2014 edition is held in the archive and downloadable from this record.

page_count_correction.ruling: MANUS: "pearl is not an 84 page collection… perhaps the core is 84 pages… but THE APPARATUS IS ALSO THE POEM, thats the whole point of pearl, and a reading that missed that has missed the point." The 84-page figure counted the verse and discarded the apparatus. The contents show why that is not a rounding error: the front matter contains an Introduction by Johannes Sigil, "from THE CRIMSON HEXAGON" attributed to Jack Feist AND to Lee Sharks, a WIKI ARTICLE, an ALSO BY page and a Contributor Bio — and the body runs PEARL with three Undersongs and a "Footnote to PEARL: belief & technique for telepathic prose". The undersongs and footnotes are not commentary on the poem; they are the poem. The 84/155 conflict between #329 and #330 is resolved in favour of 155, and the resolution is interpretive rather than arithmetic.

MACHINE-FACING TEXT ADDED, ADDITIVE ONLY. A whitespace-faithful plain-text rendering of the whole book was generated from per-word PDF geometry (character grid; gap-based intra-line spacing; run-snapped leading) and registered as an attachment beside the PDF, with the renderer committed at scripts/render_pearl_machine_text.py. The canonical text and mint bytes are untouched: the PDF is the artwork, the machine text is the score, and a facsimile deposit's record may gain surfaces but never lose or alter its sealed core. Rendering verified against page rasters (title spread p.29, Undersong III p.47, bio field p.20) before registration. Known ceiling stated in the file header: integer rows cannot distinguish 1.5x from 2x leading.

attachments.description: The full 155-page book rendered from per-word PDF geometry onto a character grid (scripts/render_pearl_machine_text.py), so lineation, indentation, and each page's vertical field survive extraction. Built because the PDF's text stream embeds tab+CR after every word — a composition artifact that defeats flow-based extraction. Leading is quantized to whole text rows at the document body pitch with near-equal gap runs snapped to their median; the PDF remains the artwork, this file is the score.
The 2014 book as published (155-page merged PDF, born-digital). Typography, lineation, spacing and image are central to the poetics; this file is canonical for how the pages look.
